items.text: 5 spooky Washington DC stories to get you in the Halloween spirit
items.article: From the White House to the U.S. Capitol, explore five of Washington, DC's most famous ghost stories and the history behind the city's haunted legends. Washington DC is known for its monuments, museums and political history. But the nation's capital also has plenty of ghost stories and haunted legends. From the White House to the U.S. Capitol, some of the city's most famous buildings are said to have ghostly visitors. Georgetown, one of Washington's oldest neighborhoods, has its own collection of spooky stories, while the Octagon House is often considered one of the city's most haunted places. Ford's Theatre, forever linked to the assassination of President Abraham Lincoln, has also become part of DC's haunted lore. Whether you believe in ghosts or not, these stories offer a different way to look at some of the capital's most familiar places.

items.article: Shares of PB Fintech have fallen 48% over six sessions due to proposed insurance commission changes. Brokerages have revised estimates, raising concerns about profitability in general insurance and the POSP model. Bernstein cut its target price by 53%. Shares of PB Fintech , the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, have been under intense selling pressure, extending their losing streak to six consecutive sessions and falling around 48% during the period. The sharp decline has come as investors reassess the potential impact of proposed changes to insurance commissions and distribution economics. The stock hit its 52-week low of ₹ 965 on October 1. It has now tanked over 50% from its 52-week high of ₹ 1,963.00, hit in December last year. The scrip has shed 42% in 3 months, 31% in 6 months and 41% in the last 1 year. The sell-off has raised concerns over the earnings outlook for insurance intermediaries, particularly companies that rely on commissions and distribution fees. Several brokerages have since revised their estimates or valuation assumptions for PB Fintech, with concerns centred on the extent to which the proposed regulatory changes could affect its general insurance and point-of-sales person (POSP) businesses. items.text: SF's favorite ice cream sandwich just made a big change
items.article: The mint flavor of San Francisco's favorite It's-It ice cream cookie sandwiches has changed color. A major change has come for San Francisco’s beloved It’s-It ice cream sandwiches. The mint flavor of the ice cream cookie sandwich , once an ostentatiously loud shade of green, has changed color, as first spotted by the San Francisco Chronicle. (The Chronicle and SFGATE are both owned by Hearst but have separate newsrooms.) An SFGATE editor bought a box at Andronico’s and confirmed the breaking news — the bright, toothpaste-green ice cream had been drained of color, with a far more muted, pale pastel green in its place. Where the shade once screamed “GREEN!” at the top of its lungs, now, it only whispered. Curiously, though, It’s-It has mostly kept the change quiet. Despite SFGATE’s repeated attempts this week to reach the Burlingame-based company for comment, It’s-It never got back to us. The company has not released any statement announcing the change to its customers, and photos of the mint ice cream sandwich on its website remain the same , advertising the old seafoam green color instead of the new, lighter shade. It’s-It President Charles Shamieh did speak with the Chronicle, telling the outlet that It’s-It made the change due to U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. items.article: CBC News breaks down each of the referendum questions to help voters prepare to mark the 10 ballots. The clock is ticking down to Alberta's provincewide referendum on 10 questions, with polls set to open at 9 a.m. on Monday, Oct. 19. Five of those questions are related to immigration, while four propose constitutional changes — each of these are "yes" or "no" questions. The final question has to do with the future of Alberta independence. Voters will be asked to choose only one of two options: for the province to stay in Canada, or to hold a second binding referendum on separating from the country. CBC News has reported extensively on the questions to help voters prepare before marking the 10 ballots.
